entry.title: On the maximum interval index of a graph
entry.summary: For a connected graph P G on n vertices, the interval index is defined by Int(G) = {u,v} subset V(G) (|I(u, v)| - 1), where I(u, v) denotes the set of all vertices lying on a shortest u - v path. It was conjectured that, among all connected graphs on n vertices, the path Pn attains the maximum value of the interval index. In this paper we settle this conjecture, and we prove that the maximum is attained only for Pn, except for n = 4, when the cycle C4 attains the same value. We also prove that, for every n >= 31, the maximum interval index among graphs without pendant vertices equals (n^3 - n)/6 - 2(n - 4) and it is attained by a dumbbell graph, obtained by joining two 4-cycles by a path.

entry.title: Dense Minors from the Crux
entry.summary: Let $G$ be a graph with average degree $d>0$ and $C_α(G)$ be the minimum order of a subgraph whose average degree is at least $αd$ for any fixed $0<α<1$. Then $G$ has a minor of average degree $Ω(\sqrt{d\,C_α(G)})$, which is asymptotically tight up to a constant factor. This reveals a unified mechanism underlying previous results on dense minors in locally sparse graphs.

entry.title: On self-similar random quotients of the line
entry.summary: A surprisingly wide variety of important random fractal metric spaces in modern probability theory can be viewed as self-similar random quotients of the real line, including the continuum random tree, Liouville quantum gravity surfaces, the trace of Brownian motion in $\mathbb{R}^d$, and self-similar ($s=2d$) long-range percolation on $\mathbb{R}$. We prove that the metric and resistance growth dimensions are well-defined in a certain sense for every random metric space in a class containing all of the above examples. Our results are new for the trace of Brownian motion.

entry.title: Level Crossing Rate Bounds for Products of Independent Nonstationary Fading Processes
entry.summary: We develop a unified framework for the instantaneous total level crossing rate (LCR) of products of independent positive nonstationary fading processes. Universal upper and lower bounds are first derived from an exact decomposition of the product derivative and signed crossing imbalance, requiring only factor-wise crossing statistics. We then introduce the drifting Gaussian-derivative (DGD) class, in which each conditional derivative is Gaussian with possibly nonzero drift. For products of DGD factors, an exact Gaussian-mixture representation yields bounds that jointly capture aggregate drift and derivative fluctuations. The lower bound reduces under stationarity to a known $\ell_2$ bound, whereas, to the best of the author's knowledge, the upper bound is new even in the stationary case. Furthermore, the bounds are asymptotically exact in drift-dominated regimes. The framework is specialized to nonstationary Double-Rayleigh fading and to quasi-identically distributed DGD factors, with closed forms for products of $α$-$μ$ envelopes. Numerical results show that the DGD bounds closely bracket the exact LCR.

entry.title: Block-exchange descent for insertion: commuting projections and minimum masks
entry.summary: For fixed nonempty words $u,v$, the minimum insertion degree of a shuffle is the least number of inserted-source runs among its representations. We prove that, after a block exchange from a minimum mask of degree $r$, the minimum over masks with commuting source projections is exactly $r-1$; a larger decrease occurs precisely when a noncommuting mask has fewer runs. If either source is unary, every such exchange is exact. We prove an explicit repair for an infinite periodic degree-three family. Computer-assisted results establish first-mask descent through combined length seventeen over every alphabet, degree-three first-mask descent through length thirty, and a uniform repair of all degree-three failures through length thirty, including all further letter identifications. Counterexamples to arbitrary, first, and last minimum-mask choices explain the need for alternative masks. Finally, we prove that minimum iteration depths have no gaps for arbitrary languages. General block-exchange descent and Singleton No-Gap remain open.
entry.arxiv:comment: 22 pages, 10 tables. Software and verification data: https://github.com/the-omega-institute/insertion-degree-descent/releases/tag/v1.0

entry.title: A New Invariant for Doubly Periodic Solutions of the Sinh-Gordon Equation
entry.summary: Spectral curves of constant mean curvature tori in Euclidean three-space are real hyperelliptic curves carrying two meromorphic differentials with integral periods. These transcendental period conditions are studied through Whitham deformations, which deform the curve while preserving the periods. We extend Whitham deformations to all real hyperelliptic curves of this type, by holding fixed the plane spanned by the periods, or this plane together with its complex structure. Under mild nondegeneracy conditions the resulting isoperiodic sets are manifolds of dimensions three and one, respectively. Along the one-dimensional isoperiodic sets, a generalization of the Willmore energy is a local parameter away from its critical points, to which the spectral curves of tori belong. Finally, using homology bases adapted to the branch points, we find discrete invariants of the isoperiodic sets of doubly periodic curves: a triple of integers and a refined conformal type.

entry.title: On record behaviours of returns for interval maps
entry.summary: Given a dynamical system $(X,T)$ and an ergodic invariant measure $μ$, a $μ$-typical point $x\in X$ under $T$ visits arbitrarily small neighbourhood of $x$. We will use techniques based on extreme value theory and Laplace functional for point process to show that, for interval maps with suitable mixing and anti-clustering conditions, the limiting distributions of the record times and values of the return process $Y_j(x)=-\log d(T^jx,x)$, after possible normalisation, has Poisson-type laws.

entry.title: Lie point symmetry analysis of a dependent jump-diffusion risk model with exponential claim sizes
entry.summary: We carry out a Lie point symmetry analysis of the coupled integro-differential system satisfied by the conditional Gerber--Shiu functions of a dependent jump-diffusion risk model. In the model, claim sizes are exponential, the intensity of the next claim arrival depends on whether the current claim exceeds a random threshold, and both the volatility and the premium rate may depend on the surplus. We write the system as the restriction to the half-line of a far-field operator with prescribed exterior data, derive the complete set of determining equations, including the condition imposed by the nonlocal convolution term, and solve them. The resulting group classification holds for every surplus-dependent volatility and premium of the form considered and for every absolutely continuous or constant threshold distribution. A non-trivial symmetry beyond scaling and superposition exists if and only if the volatility and the premium rate are constant, and it is then exactly the translation in the surplus variable. We construct the optimal system of one-dimensional subalgebras. We show that the invariant solutions of the combined translation--scaling generators exist precisely when a $2\times2$ generalized Lundberg determinant vanishes, and we give this determinant for an arbitrary threshold distribution, with explicit forms for the constant and exponential thresholds. We prove existence and sign properties of the adjustment coefficient, derive its sensitivities to all model parameters, and establish Cramér--Lundberg-type asymptotics for the Gerber--Shiu functions, including the limit of the ratio between the two regimes. A numerical study shows that claim-size-driven dependence lowers the adjustment coefficient markedly below that of an independent model with the same mean claim intensity.

entry.title: Low-rank matrices with three prescribed off-diagonal values over $\mathbb{F}_p$
entry.summary: Let $p$ be a prime such that $2$ is a primitive root modulo $p$. We prove that, for every three-element set $L\subseteq\mathbb{F}_p$ and every integer $n\geq1$, there exists a symmetric $n\times n$ matrix over $\mathbb{F}_p$ with zero diagonal, off-diagonal entries in $L$, and rank $O_{p,L}(n^{1/3})$. This answers a question of Bukh for all such primes and, in particular, settles the case $L=\{1,4,6\}\subseteq\mathbb{F}_{19}$ singled out on his problem list. When $0\notin L$, a standard polynomial argument shows that the exponent $1/3$ is optimal. The proof combines a geometric construction in characteristic two with an incidence matrix factorization over $\mathbb{F}_p$. The same construction yields integer lifts $L'$ of the prescribed sets $L$ and symmetric $L'$-matrices of rational rank $O_{p,L}(n^{1/3})$. When $0\notin L'$, this improves Bukh's general quadratic lower bound, giving matrices of order $Ω_{p,L}(r^3)$ and rational rank at most $r$.

entry.title: Interacting particles in random irregular media
entry.summary: In this paper, we first develop novel tools of independent interest in the field of stochastic calculus related to SDEs with distributional drift, namely the formulation of a quasi-Stroock-Varadhan martingale problem in the sense that the test functions are of class $C^{1,2}$ instead of solutions of Kolmogorov type PDE. This has several applications, among which, the time restriction and the notion of conditional rough martingale problem and related solution.

entry.title: The asymptotic number of zonotopes
entry.summary: We provide a sharp estimate for the asymptotic number of lattice zonotopes inscribed in [0, n] d as n tends to infinity. Our estimate refines the logarithmic equivalent established by B{á}r{á}ny, Bureaux, and Lund when the sum of the generators of the zonotope is prescribed. As we shall see, the exponential part of our estimate is a polynomial of degree d in n 1/(d+1) , plus a term involving the non-trivial zeros of the Riemann zeta function. Our analysis is based on a correspondence between power sums over primitive vectors (vectors with coprime coordinates) and Eulerian polynomials. We also analyse some combinatorial properties of lattice zonotopes. In particular, we compute the asymptotic mean and variance of the diameter of the graph of a random lattice zonotope inscribed in [0, n] d as n goes to infinity, and show that this diameter satisfies a central limit theorem.

entry.title: Strong rate for one-dimensional driftless continuous strict local martingales
entry.summary: For one-dimensional strict local martingales of the form $\mathrm{d} X_t=σ(X_t) \mathrm{d} W_t$ starting from $X_{0}=x_{0}>0$, we prove the strong rate $\mathbb{E}\left[|X^h_N-X_T|\right] \lesssim h^{\min\{θα,\frac{1}{2}\}}$ for a discrete scheme~$X^h$ truncated at a level $h^{-α}$, with time step~$h$, as $h\downarrow 0$, where~$θ$ depends on the truncation property. For the CEV model $σ(x)\equiv x^{1+γ}$ in particular, the rate is~$\frac{1}{2}$ for any $γ\in (0,1)$ (up to a logarithmic pre-factor at $γ=\frac{1}{2}$).

entry.title: Planarity estimates and codimension reduction for ancient flows at the Andrews-Baker threshold
entry.summary: We derive an interior planarity estimate for space-time proper mean curvature flows of $n$-dimensional submanifolds of $\mathbb R^{n+p}$, $n\geq5$, that are uniformly quadratically pinched up to the Andrews-Baker threshold $\frac{4}{3n}$. The estimate is parabolically scale-invariant and it requires neither curvature nor entropy bounds. The proof combines Naff's gradient estimates with a localization argument in the spirit of Ecker and Huisken. In dimensions five and six, Naff's estimates alone do not give the gradient terms a sign. We bound these terms from below with an argument we developed in a previous work. As a consequence, for $n\geq5$, and by known results for $2\leq n\leq4$, every space-time proper ancient solution that is uniformly $\frac{4}{3n}$-pinched is either a static affine $n$-plane or lies in a fixed affine $(n+1)$-dimensional subspace. This replaces the finite entropy and polynomial curvature growth assumptions of Lee, Naff and Zhu by space-time properness, and improves their pinching constant in dimensions two, five and six. For closed flows, we extend Lynch's planarity estimate to a larger range of exponents.

entry.title: Isospectral congruence manifolds, spectral rigidity, and a converse to Vignéras
entry.summary: Let $B$ be a quaternion division algebra over a number field $k$ that gives rise to arithmetic Fuchsian or Kleinian groups, and let $\mathcal{O}$ be a maximal order of $B$. We show that every closed orientable Riemannian manifold isospectral to a principal congruence hyperbolic surface $X_\mathcal{O}(\mathfrak{a})$ is isometric to $X_{\mathcal{O}'}(\mathfrak{a})$ for some maximal order $\mathcal{O}'$ of $B$, provided that no prime factor of $\mathfrak{a}$ ramifies in $B$ and that $\mathfrak{a}$ satisfies a mild condition at the primes over $2$. This is a converse to the construction of Vignéras, which produces isospectral manifolds from maximal orders of different types. In particular the spectral genus of $X_\mathcal{O}(\mathfrak{a})$ has at most $t(B)$ elements, and $X_\mathcal{O}(\mathfrak{a})$ is spectrally rigid when the type number $t(B)$ is one. In dimension three we prove the same statements for manifolds that, in addition, have the same complex lengths of closed geodesics. The proof rests on a local result that characterizes, by traces alone, the subgroups of $\mathrm{SL}(2)$ over a $p$-adic ring that are conjugate into a principal congruence subgroup by traces. As applications, every principal congruence Hurwitz surface is spectrally rigid, among them Klein's quartic, the Fricke-Macbeath surface and the surfaces of the first Hurwitz triplet, which partially answers a question of Reid.

entry.title: Optimal self-orthogonal binary linear codes
entry.summary: We complete the determination of the minimum possible length of eight-dimensional binary self-orthogonal codes with given minimum distance. For dimension nine we give exact values and bounds for minimum distance at most $64$. By exploiting the geometric reformulation of linear codes as multisets of points, we fully redo the classification for dimension at most seven in a simplified and computer-free manner. As a by-product we prove the non-existence of $[93,9,44]_2$ codes and show several divisibility results for putative optimal nine-dimensional binary codes.

entry.title: From Trees to Binary Trees: Approximation Algorithms and a PTAS
entry.summary: Kellerhals, Krebs, Nichterlein, and Schmid introduced the optimization problem Tree in Binary Tree (TBT), where, given a tree $T$, the task is to find a binary tree $S^*$ with $V(T)=V(S^*)$ that minimizes $\sum_{uv\in E(T)} \operatorname{dist}_{S^*}(u,v)$. They also introduced the variant Tree in Binary Tree With Steiner Nodes (TBT-SN), where the condition $V(T)=V(S^*)$ is relaxed to $V(T)\subseteq V(S^*)$. We give a simple linear-time $\frac{8}{3}$-approximation algorithm for TBT and a polynomial-time approximation scheme (PTAS) for TBT-SN. Our main building idea in both algorithms is to iteratively consider subtrees of the tree $T$ which contain all vertices below some vertex $v$ and construct a solution where $v$ has degree 1. For the PTAS, we cut $T$ into smaller trees, solve these instances, modify the obtained solutions, and combine them to achieve a solution for the original instance.

entry.title: Exact Avoid-or-Compress Extrema for Dense Reachable Images: Defects Four and Five
entry.summary: Let $S$ be a reachable image of a strongly connected synchronizing automaton and $\varnothing\ne A\subsetneq S$. We determine the maximum shortest avoid-or-compress length over binary and arbitrary finite alphabets for $m=n-|S|=4$ and $m=5$. The exact values are $\min(n-|A|,11)$ and $\min(n-|A|,14)$, respectively. Uniform binary constructions attain both bounds. For the upper bounds, short-pair graphs and actual-image constraints reduce all parameters to finite necessary domains. Exhaustive checks exclude the domains, apart from a single relaxation eliminated by a multipartite overlap lemma. The largest calculation covers 3,206,988 domains.
entry.arxiv:comment: 13 pages, 2 figures, 1 table. Computer-assisted upper bounds

entry.title: On the geometry of asymptotically conical Ricci shrinkers (I): weighted analysis
entry.summary: We develop the weighted Sobolev and Hölder analysis needed to study perturbations of complete asymptotically conical (AC) Ricci shrinkers. Weighted elliptic estimates yield a global weighted divergence-free slice in spaces that retain the asymptotic data at infinity. As a geometric application, we prove pointed Gromov-Hausdorff rigidity of nontrivial AC shrinkers with vanishing infinitesimal solitonic deformation space.

entry.title: PDE-based Bayesian Inverse Problems in All-at-once Framework
entry.summary: We propose a modern all-at-once framework for PDE-based Bayesian inversion by introducing the PDE residual as probabilistic information. In this framework, the PDE residual is treated as a soft constraint with a residual covariance and is directly incorporated into the likelihood function. The new hybrid likelihood function eliminates PDE solves, thus reducing expensive computational costs, while performing rigorous Bayesian inference. Theoretically, we establish the well-posedness of the posterior with uncertainty quantification, and numerically, we propose two efficiency inversion algorithms based on two posterior sampling methods. In particular, one algorithm is based on Metropolis-within-Gibbs MCMC method with a PDE-informed block- diagonal Gaussian prior, and the other is based on a joint sampling strategy. Numerical experiments for a semiconductor inverse problem confirm that the proposed Bayesian all-at-once approach yields a speedup of approximately a factor of two, while having a comparable reconstruction quality as the conventional reduced-based setting.

entry.title: Functional limit theorems for Galton-Watson processes with inhomogeneous immigration towards a deterministic limit function
entry.summary: We study the asymptotic behavior of a sequence of Galton-Watson processes with inhomogeneous immigration when the limit of the means of the offspring distributions is equal to 1. Under a growth condition on the variances of the offspring distributions, assuming the locally uniform convergence of the expectation functions of properly scaled immigration processes towards a càdlàg function, and the locally uniform convergence of the mean absolute deviation functions of the scaled immigration processes in question towards zero, we establish a functional limit theorem for the sequence of Galton-Watson processes with inhomogeneous immigration in question towards a deterministic limit process. We also provide some applications, among others, we show that a recent result of Rahimov and Sharipov (2024) on a functional limit theorem for a sequence of nearly critical Galton-Watson processes with dependent immigration can be recovered using our result.

entry.title: EPPA for Reducts of the Random Graph
entry.summary: We prove that finite two-graphs have coherent EPPA and that neither graphs modulo global complementation nor two-graphs modulo global complementation have EPPA. This completes the classification of EPPA and coherent EPPA for the reducts of the random graph, answering a question and confirming a conjecture of Evans, Hubička, Konečný and Nešetřil.

entry.title: Minimum-degree thresholds beyond bounded colourability
entry.summary: We survey recent developments on minimum-degree thresholds in extremal graph theory, with an emphasis on structural refinements of the chromatic-threshold problem. The chromatic threshold asks when a linear minimum-degree condition forces bounded chromatic number in an \(H\)-free graph; its complete classification shows a striking finite trichotomy. We discuss several stronger and related threshold notions in which bounded colourability is replaced by bounded \(H\)-free homomorphic images, bounded neighbourhood complexity via VC-dimension, exact blowup structure for maximal \(H\)-free graphs, and improved quantitative bounds in graph removal lemmas. In contrast with the rigidity of the chromatic threshold, these newer parameters exhibit richer behaviour, including separations from \(δ_χ(H)\), new exact values, accumulation points in fixed-chromatic spectra, positivity phenomena for 3-chromatic graphs, asymmetric variants, and failures of monotonicity.
entry.arxiv:comment: Survey article. Accepted for publication in the Proceedings of the International Consortium of Chinese Mathematicians (ICCM 2025)

entry.title: Four-Coloring Planar Graphs in Linear Time
entry.summary: The famous Four Color Theorem (4CT) states that any planar graph can be colored with four colors, but how do we find a 4-coloring? In our previous paper [FOCS'26], we presented a simple combinatorial algorithm to 4-color planar graphs in $O(n\log n)$ time. We improve it here to $O(n)$ time, which is optimal. The algorithm from our previous paper is based on proving that every planar triangulation has a linear number of reducible configurations or obstructing cycles. The bottleneck for the algorithm is that we need $O(\log n)$ Kempe changes to extend a recursive 4-coloring to the reducible configurations. Each Kempe change can involve a constant fraction of the graph and takes linear time. Here we show that all $O(\log n)$ Kempe changes can be identified and implemented in $O(n)$ time. The idea is to spend $O(n)$ time to preprocess the graph so that we can identify and simulate each good Kempe change in $O(n/\log n)$ amortized time. Thus, we implement all $O(\log n)$ Kempe changes in $O(n)$ total time. Based on this, we implement the whole 4-coloring in linear time. We note that creating such a representation for fast identification and simulation of the right Kempe changes is a challenge of data structures, unlike the previous paper that builds on a new graph theoretic understanding of reducible configurations.

entry.title: The Berry--Esseen estimate in the Boolean central limit theorem
entry.summary: We estimate the Lévy distance to the symmetric Bernoulli distribution for normalized Boolean convolution powers of a probability measure with mean zero and variance one. If the absolute moment of order $r$ is finite, we obtain the upper bounds $o(n^{-(r-2)/6})$ for $2<r<5$ and $O(n^{-1/2})$ for $r\ge5$. The proof relies on an inequality that controls the Lévy distance to the Bernoulli law by the values of the reciprocal Cauchy transform at two points. For each $r\ge2$, we also construct a single fixed distribution whose absolute moments are finite exactly up to order $r$, and show that the exponent $\min\{(r-2)/6,1/2\}$ cannot be improved. Under only a finite second moment assumption, the convergence can be arbitrarily slow.

entry.title: Random semigroups á la Gromov
entry.summary: We introduce a model of random semigroups analogous to Gromov's density model for random groups. For a fixed number $n\ge 2$ of generators and a density parameter $δ\in (0,1)$, we impose a uniformly chosen set of $\lfloor n^{2δl}\rfloor$ relations of the form $u=v$, where $u,v$ are distinct words of length at most $l$, and study the resulting semigroup as $l\to\infty$. We prove that, with overwhelming probability, above density $1/2$ the semigroup is trivial, while below density $1/2$ it contains a free subsemigroup of rank two, has a Golod-Shafarevich semigroup algebra over every field, and has a homomorphic image which generates a non-elementary hyperbolic group. We also show that the small cancellation condition $C(m)$ holds with overwhelming probability whenever $δ<1/2m$. Finally, for $n\ge 3$, at critical density $1/2$ we obtain a subsequential limiting distribution on finite semigroups, with positive mass at the trivial semigroup and unbounded support in size. This contrasts with random groups, which have order at most two with overwhelming probability at critical density.

entry.title: A new sharp Sobolev inequality between the $Q$-curvature and the scalar curvature on Euclidean space
entry.summary: We establish a sharp Sobolev-type inequality on $\mathbb{R}^n$, $n\geq 5$, that interpolates between the second-order energy and a weighted first-order term. Specifically, we determine the sharp constant $S_{4,2}$ in the inequality \begin{equation*} \int_{\mathbb R^n} (Δu)^2\,dx \ge S_{4,2} \left(\int_{\mathbb{R}^n}|\nabla u|^{2}|u|^{\frac{4}{n-4}}\,dx\right)^{\frac{n-4}{n-2}}, \end{equation*} for any $u\in\dot H^2(\mathbb{R}^n)$, and we classify the cases of equality. This solves the problem of minimizing the total $Q$-curvature of among metrics on the sphere, conformal to the standard metric, with fixed total scalar curvature.

entry.title: On edge-ordered Ramsey numbers of hypergraphs
entry.summary: For an integer $h\geq2$, an edge-ordered $h$-uniform hypergraph $H^<$ is an $h$-uniform hypergraph with a linear ordering of its hyperedges. For an integer $q \geq 1$, the edge-ordered Ramsey number $R_{\mathrm{edge}}(H^<;q)$ of $H^<$ is the smallest positive integer $N$ such that there exists an edge-ordered $h$-uniform hypergraph $G^<$ on $N$ vertices such that, for every $q$-coloring of the hyperedges of $G^<$, there is a monochromatic copy of $H^<$ in $G^<$ preserving the hyperedge order. In this note, we show that, for every edge-ordered $h$-uniform hypergraph $F^<$ on $n$ vertices with $m\geq1$ hyperedges, $R_{\mathrm{edge}}(F^<;q) \leq R_h(F;q)^{Cm^2}$ where $F$ is the underlying unordered hypergraph, $R_h(F;q)$ is its standard $q$-color Ramsey number, and $C=C(h,q)>0$ is a constant. For fixed $h\geq3$ and $q\geq2$, this shows that prescribing the hyperedge order does not require an increase in the tower height of the classical upper bound. It also settles a problem posed by Fox and Li (2020), and for $h=2$ gives the bound $2^{O(n^4\log n)}$, improving their bounds for every fixed $q \geq 3$.

entry.title: Lipschitz regularity of Sobolev maps from $\mathrm{RCD}(K,N)$ spaces to $\mathrm{CAT}(0)$ spaces
entry.summary: We establish a quantitative criterion for local Lipschitz regularity of Sobolev maps in the sense of Korevaar and Schoen from finite-dimensional \(\RCD(K,N)\) spaces into complete \(\CAT(0)\) spaces, without assuming harmonicity. We quantify the failure of local energy minimality by the harmonic replacement potential, a dyadic sum of the square roots of normalized energy gaps between a map and its harmonic replacements. We prove that this potential, together with an averaged energy term, controls the minimal weak upper gradient pointwise, with constants depending only on the curvature-dimension bounds and the scale. In particular, local boundedness of the replacement potential implies that the map admits a locally Lipschitz representative.

entry.title: Solutions to several problems on infinite sumset configurations
entry.summary: We resolve a number of the problems collected by Kra, Moreira, Richter and Robertson in their survey "Problems on infinite sumset configurations in the integers and beyond". Our main result is that in every countably infinite abelian group, every set of positive upper Banach density contains a sumset $B_1+\dots+B_k$ of $k$ infinite sets, for every $k$; the proof uses the Kronecker factor, but no higher-order Host-Kra structure theory, nilsystems of step greater than one, or nilspaces. We also answer, positively or negatively, questions on monochromatic sets $B+mB$, on sumsets in sets of logarithmic density, on polynomial sumset configurations, on sums of the form $B_{i_1}+\dots+B_{i_m}$ with $B_i$ drawn from a density family, on random sets, on ordered sumsets in shifted primes, on sums and products in $\mathbb{N}$ and $\mathbb{Q}$, and on sumsets in abelian groups. Several of these answers concern the questions as literally stated, and two follow directly from known examples; in each case we say so and discuss the natural corrected question. Finally, answering a question of Kousek and Radić, we show that the supremum of the lower Banach densities of sets $A\subset\mathbb{N}$ such that $B+B+t\not\subset A$ for every infinite $B\subset\mathbb{N}$ and every $t\ge0$ (respectively $B+B\not\subset A$ for every infinite $B$) is $1/2$ (respectively $3/4$). The main theorem and most of the other results are formalized in Lean 4, with some published theorems entering as explicit hypotheses.

entry.title: Symbolic depth functions of edge ideals via local graph structure
entry.summary: We study the depth of symbolic powers of edge ideals, focusing on local properties of graphs. First, we give several sufficient conditions for the symbolic depth function to be non-increasing, using local properties of graphs and local cohomology. Next, we give a counterexample to a conjecture of Minh, T.N. Trung, and Vu concerning the stable value of the symbolic depth function, where the difference between the conjectured value and the actual value can be arbitrary large. Finally, we study a conjecture of Muta stating the depth of a symbolic power of an edge ideal is at least that of the corresponding ordinary power. We prove it for graphs whose connected components are unicyclic or bipartite.

entry.title: Emergence of the transformer architecture as the score of entropic laws of random measures
entry.summary: We show that the transformer architecture emerges as the score of last-token laws in a natural statistical model of language, where sentences are empirical measures of tokens, a language is a law on $P(S^d)$, and our prior belief is that sentences carry no structure at all. By the maximum-entropy principle, we select the law closest to this prior in relative entropy among those reproducing an observed sentence-level statistic. We discuss the relevance of the statistic in the posterior interaction between tokens and we build a statistic, able to capture that interaction, with Luce's choice axiom truncated at the lowest relational order. This procedure gives the softmax choice rule, with the attention cross-moment as its mean parameter. The query--key matrix is then the Lagrange multiplier of a maximum-entropy problem inside each sentence, and the value matrix the multiplier of the constraint over the language, so that the two are untied. Under the optimal entropic law we then show that a transformer head appears in the score of the last-token law. For ordered sentences, causal masking follows from the masked reference choice rule, and with a next-token cross-moment the score equals one causally masked attention head. We also discuss multi-head attention, weight-tied unembedding, and a heuristic reading of residual blocks as projected Langevin steps.

entry.title: Fractal dimensions of paths on three-dimensional random-walk traces
entry.summary: We study four paths that join the starting site to the final position of a simple random walk of \(N=L^2\) steps on the infinite cubic lattice. The paths are selected on the walk trace---the graph of visited sites and traversed bonds---by different rules: the undirected shortest path \(S_1\), the directed shortest path \(S_2\), the time-respecting shortest path \(S_3\), and the depth \(D_e\) of the final site in a depth-first-search tree. Monte Carlo simulations for \(L\) up to 32768 give mean lengths scaling as \(L^{d_O}\), with \(d_{S_1}=1.48005(9)\), \(d_{S_2}=1.49868(5)\), \(d_{S_3}=1.51205(5)\), and \(d_{D_e}=1.7099(7)\), so that \(d_{S_1}<d_{S_2}<d_{S_3}<d_{\rm LE}<d_{D_e}\), where $d_{\rm LE}=1.62400(5)$ is the known loop-erased-random-walk exponent. Imposing traversal directions increases the shortest-path exponent, and imposing time order increases it further; these constraints therefore change the scaling exponent, not only the amplitude. For every path, the standard deviation scales with the same exponent as the mean, so it is scale-invariant, unlike the visited-site mass; the rescaled length distributions collapse onto a finite-width scaling function. No analytical theory currently predicts these exponents; our results provide precise numerical benchmarks for future studies of path geometry on random-walk traces.

entry.title: Tiling circular $n$-boards with squares and (1,1)-fences
entry.summary: We show that the number of ways to tile a circular $n$-board (an annulus divided into $n$ curved unit square cells) with appropriately curved unit squares and curved (1,1)-fences is a Lucas number squared if $n$ is even and an odd-indexed Lucas number otherwise. A curved (1,1)-fence is composed of two curved unit squares separated by a gap in the shape of another curved unit square. This combinatorial interpretation of the Lucas numbers squared and the odd-indexed Lucas numbers allows us to obtain various identities concerning these sequences in a quick and lucid manner.

entry.title: The number of $C_4$-free graphs
entry.summary: Erdős, Frankl and Rödl showed that the number of graphs on $n$ vertices with no copy of a non-bipartite graph $H$ is $2^{(1+o(1))ex(n,H)}$, whereas Morris and Saxton showed that this fails for $C_6$. Answering a question of Erdős, we prove that the number of $C_4$-free graphs on $n$ vertices is $2^{(1+o(1))ex(n,C_4)}$. The proof combines a modified hypergraph container method that treats pairs of vertices with large codegree separately, with a new bound on the number of matchings in a graph.

entry.title: Topological Insights and Combinatorial Frameworks for Twist Knot Complements
entry.summary: The complement of a knot in $\mathbb{S}^3$ is a fundamental object in $3$-manifold topology and serves as a primary building block in the study of geometric structures on manifolds. For a large class of knots, these complements admit complete hyperbolic metrics, motivating the development of various frameworks for their classification and analysis. A twist knot is formed by applying a series of half-twists to a closed loop and linking the ends. In this article, we present explicit topological and combinatorial descriptions of all twist knot complements via the construction of suitable cell structures. Our method produces a closed $3$-dimensional pseudomanifold with a single vertex, arising from prescribed face pairings of a faceted $3$-ball. Removing the vertex yields the complement of the corresponding twist knot. The construction naturally induces ideal triangulations of these knot complements, several of which are shown to be facet-minimal. Beyond providing concrete models, our approach offers new perspectives on the topology of knot complements and leads to some open research problems.
